title: Memory
final_note: You worked through the key terms in Memory.

concepts.def: Atkinson and Shiffrin's 1968 model of memory with sensory register, short-term and long-term stores.
The process of converting information into a form that can be stored in memory (acoustic, visual, semantic).
War of the Ghosts study showed memory is reconstructive; participants altered the story to fit their own schemas.
Found STM duration is around 18 seconds when rehearsal is prevented using trigrams.
Forgetting due to absence of cues; explained by Tulving's encoding specificity principle.
Forgetting because one memory blocks another, causing distortion; proactive or retroactive.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Memory — a core area of GCSE Psychology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Memory brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Memory.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: How long does information typically last in short-term memory without rehearsal, according to Peterson and Peterson?
Whose 1932 'War of the Ghosts' study demonstrated reconstructive memory?

numericals.q: In what year did Atkinson and Shiffrin propose the multi-store model?

free_texts.q: Whose 1932 study used War of the Ghosts to show reconstructive memory?
free_texts.hint: Cambridge psychologist, surname begins with B.
